column1: # clues.tsv for ft_fibonacci — pedagogic hints only. NEVER state the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><member CASE label><TAB>...   (fires if ANY member case fails)
# Lines are shown most-fundamental first; the first line doubles as the "foothold".

Every recursion needs somewhere to stop. What are the two smallest indices the sequence defines directly, and what value does each of them stand for? If these are wrong, nothing built on top of them can be right.
Each later term is built from the two terms just before it. Which two, and how are they combined? Make sure your recursive calls actually move toward the base cases rather than away from them.

An index below zero has no term in the sequence. What single sentinel value is the agreed way to report that error, and does every negative input — including the most extreme one — reach that same path?
